notes: Company overview: national omnichannel retailer (apparel + home), heavy seasonal peaks (Black Friday, Holiday). CS volume spikes 7-10x.
Primary problem: agents waste time toggling between systems; refunds require 3 API calls + manager approval in many cases -> high handle time.
Goal: agent assist + automated tool-calls to create/update tickets, initiate refunds, and flag escalations to L2 via API hooks.
Must-haves: idempotent tool-calls (duplicate protection), per-call audit log, end-to-end traceability tying LLM output to API ops.
Latency target: sub-500ms for assistant suggestions; <800ms end-to-end for auto-triggered refund call in interactive flows.
Throughput: baseline 2k concurrent agent sessions; peak 20k requests/min during promotions. Want reliable routing to Dedicated/Private under spikes.
Cost sensitivity: moderate; willing to pay for reserved capacity for Black Friday windows but expect Optimize suggestions to reduce token/unit cost.
Security: PCI scope concerns for refunds. Require tokenization and encryption, KMS integration, SOC2 type II. Also want SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync.
Integrations: Zendesk (tickets), Payments API v2 (refunds-service.internal), Order Management (OMS) GraphQL, PagerDuty for escalations.
Tool-calling specifics discussed: retry/backoff, exactly-once semantics via idempotency keys, webhook callbacks to update UI, signed JWT from Redwood to internal APIs.
Quote from Head of CX (call 2026-02-25): "If you can reduce HTR by 30% and guarantee no payment reversals, we can justify dedicated capacity."
SE notes: built a mock tool-caller in demo using a sandbox refunds-service; observed safe-fail path needed when payments API 429s during spikes.
Security feedback: want on-prem option for refunds routing or private deployment inside VPC to limit egress; also asked for evidence of audit logging format.
Procurement: procurement team needs estimated SLOs, indemnity for payment processing errors, and sample contract language for PO.
Next steps checklist: 1) Provide dedicated capacity pricing and blackout windows options. 2) SE to deliver POC plan + test matrix by Mar 12. 3) Security to confirm KMS/HSM support.
summary: Retailer evaluating Redwood for agent assist + tool-calling to automate refunds and escalations. Focus on reliability under large spikes, PCI scope, and idempotent API integrations. POC scheduled; primary blockers are security answers and SAML metadata.
